title: English-taught master's programmes in Germany: where to look
description: Germany offers well over a thousand master's programmes taught entirely in English. How to find them, what they cost and how the application works.
html:
You do not need German to do a master's degree in Germany. Universities have expanded their English-taught programmes for years, and today there are more than a thousand to choose from, most of them at public universities that charge no tuition. This guide explains where they are concentrated, how to find them and what to expect from the application.

Which subjects are taught in English

Engineering, computer science, data science, economics and management dominate the list, followed by the natural sciences and a growing number of programmes in the social sciences and public policy. Creative fields such as design and architecture also have English-taught options, usually at universities of applied sciences. Medicine and law remain almost entirely in German.

Where to find them

The database of the German Academic Exchange Service lists every accredited programme and lets you filter by language of instruction. Our own programme finder covers the same ground with filters for city, tuition and deadline. Once you have a shortlist, go to the university's own page for the programme: that is where the precise admission requirements and the current deadline live.

What they cost

At public universities in most federal states there is no tuition, only a semester contribution of €150 to €400 that covers administration and usually a public transport ticket. Baden-Württemberg charges non-EU students €1,500 per semester. Private universities charge from €5,000 to more than €15,000 a year. Add living costs of roughly €1,000 a month, which is also the amount the visa requires you to prove.

How the application works

Most programmes ask for a bachelor's degree in a related field with a grade above a stated threshold, an English certificate (IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL 90 are typical), a letter of motivation and a CV. Some require a GRE or GMAT score, particularly in economics. Applications go either directly to the university or through the central application service, which checks foreign certificates for a fee. Deadlines for the winter semester usually fall between January and July, and most international applicants should aim to apply by March so that the visa process has enough time.

A realistic timeline

Twelve months before the start: shortlist programmes and book your English test. Nine months before: collect transcripts and references. Six months before: apply. Three to four months before: admission letters arrive, visa application starts, Blocked Account and health insurance are set up. Two months before: visa appointment. That is tight but common, and the reason we tell everyone to start the financial side early.
